fields.reasoning: Intents: `rhiza ls --kind intent` shows only milestone intents (m3 to m31: daemon, apps, Nebari, browser monitor, root, public docs, sign-off pages); none is about CI time, and the intent itself puts the general CI speed-up (request 01M6Q58) out of scope, so attaching it to a milestone would misstate the plan; a standalone request change set needs no intent. Detection: ci.yml already checks out with fetch-depth 0 and triggers only on pull_request and workflow_dispatch (no push trigger; Ship dispatches on main commits), so git diff against the merge base is enough and avoids a new action dependency, and forcing code=true on workflow_dispatch keeps main's CI full, as the intent requires. Today `check` is the aggregate branch protection and Ship read and it rejects anything but success; it must now accept skipped, but still fail when `changes` itself failed (otherwise a broken detector would skip everything and pass). A separate `model` job instead of lint avoids running self-check twice on code PRs, and matches the intent's "builds rhiza and runs make self-check". Ship: internal/api/ship.go passingConclusions already counts SKIPPED as passing in checksVerdict, and shipRerunFailed skips passing conclusions, so no code change is expected, but nothing tests it; the intent explicitly asks to check ship check and the watchdog rerun, and a leaf with an acceptance test is the cheap way to prove it. Plan review round 2 (f1, confirmed): internal/op/fields_test.go TestEveryFieldInRepoLogIsKnown is the only Go test reading the repo's own .rhiza/log, and the only other op.FieldKnown caller is internal/api/write_node.go (on write); the model job runs it so a model-only PR loses no check it has today.
fields.statement: (1) Change set 01M7684 serves no milestone intent: it is a standalone owner request (filed 2026-11-11, "yes file it"), like the bug and request change sets beside it. Plan its leaves under it with no serves link, and do not invent an intent or a policy.toml for it. (2) ci.yml gets a first job, `changes`, that decides with plain git (checkout already uses fetch-depth 0, no third-party action): on pull_request it lists `git diff --name-only <merge-base of base.sha and head>..<head>` and outputs code=true when any path lies outside .rhiza/, else code=false; on workflow_dispatch (Ship's runs on main commits) it always outputs code=true, so main keeps running everything. lint, scripts, api, rest and budgets run only when code=true. A new `model` job runs only when code=false: it sets up Go and runs `make self-check` (build this commit's rhiza in a temp dir, rhiza check including stale .rhiza/rendered), then `go test -trimpath ./internal/op -run TestEveryFieldInRepoLogIsKnown`: that test globs the repo's .rhiza/log and fails on any node field op.FieldKnown does not know, which fold and rhiza check never validate (only writes do), so without it a log entry written by a newer or unmerged rhiza would turn a red model-only PR green. `check` stays the single required aggregate: it needs changes, model and the five Go jobs, runs if: always(), fails unless `changes` succeeded, and passes only when every other needed job is success or skipped, with at least one of `model` or the Go jobs having succeeded. make check stays the local entry point, unchanged. (3) Yes: ship check gets its own small leaf, a Go test in internal/api, proving a check rollup with SKIPPED jobs and a SUCCESS `check` is settled and green under checksVerdict, and that shipRerunFailed reruns nothing for SKIPPED runs.

fields.acceptance: Go tests in internal/ciworkflow (go test -trimpath ./internal/ciworkflow/...) parse .github/workflows/ci.yml and assert: a `changes` job with an output code, computing it from git diff --name-only against the merge base on pull_request and setting it true on workflow_dispatch; lint, scripts, api, rest and budgets each needing changes with if on code == 'true'; a `model` job needing changes with if on code == 'false' that runs make self-check and `go test -trimpath ./internal/op -run TestEveryFieldInRepoLogIsKnown` (so a model-only PR whose log carries a field op.FieldKnown rejects still fails CI, as it does today through the api/rest jobs); check needing changes, model and the five Go jobs, if: always(), failing unless changes succeeded and every other result is success or skipped, and failing when none of model and the five Go jobs succeeded (an all-skipped run fails check); the existing triggers, concurrency, matrices and cache checks still pass. make check is unchanged. The change set's own PR touches Go code so runs everything; the next model-only PR's CI completes in a few minutes with check green, read from gh run view.
fields.statement: On a pull request whose changed paths all lie under .rhiza/, CI runs only a `model` job (setup-go, make self-check, then `go test -trimpath ./internal/op -run TestEveryFieldInRepoLogIsKnown`, the one Go test that reads the repo's own .rhiza/log and fails on a node field this commit's code does not know, which neither fold nor rhiza check validates) and skips lint, scripts, api, rest and budgets, decided by a first `changes` job using plain git diff against the merge base (code=true when any path is outside .rhiza/, always true on workflow_dispatch); any other PR and every dispatched run on main runs everything as today, and the aggregate `check` job, needing changes, model and the five Go jobs with if: always(), fails unless changes succeeded and passes only when every other job is success or skipped with at least one of them succeeded.
